steps.body: A rational **equation** clears its fractions in one move: **multiply every term by the LCD**. For 3/x + 1/2 = 2 (LCD 2x): 6 + x = 4x → x = **2**. Check: 3/2 + 1/2 = 2. ✓ One multiplication, then ordinary algebra.

commonErrors.feedback: x = −6 is EXCLUDED — it zeroes a denominator; the solution is +6 (and check: 5/6 = 10/12 ✓).

steps.body: The exclusions from Chapter 1 become **candidate filters**, exactly like extraneous solutions in radical equations. Multiplying by the LCD can mint candidates that zero a denominator — those are phantoms. **Solve, then check every candidate against the banned list.**

explanationVariants: Clear by (x − 3), solve the linear result, and confirm 5 isn't banned.

commonErrors.feedback: 3 zeroes the denominators — it's the EXCLUDED value, never a solution; the honest candidate is 5.
1 + 2(x − 3) = x gives 2x − 5 = x → x = +5 — track the sign when collecting.

predict.prompt: Clearing the LCD gave candidates x = 4 and x = 7, from an equation whose denominator was (x − 4). Before checking either — can BOTH be solutions?

options.label: No — x = 4 was never allowed, because it zeroes the denominator
Yes — both came out of correct algebra, so both count
No — multiplying by the LCD invalidates every candidate

predict.reveal: Only one. x = 4 was banned before the algebra started — it makes the original denominator zero, so it was never in the domain. Multiplying by the LCD quietly removed that restriction and minted a candidate the original equation cannot accept.

widget.prompt: The solving reduces to (x − 7)/(x − 4). Build its sign chart — then look at where each candidate sits.
widget.successFeedback: There is the verdict, drawn rather than recalled: x = 7 sits ON the axis — the function is genuinely zero there, so it solves the equation. x = 4 is the dashed line, where the function does not exist at all. A solution has to be a point on the curve, and only one of the two candidates is.
widget.crossFeedback: Both cuts are odd, so the sign changes at each — at the zero (x = 7) because the curve passes through the axis, and at the pole (x = 4) because it swaps sides of the asymptote without ever touching it.
widget.bounceFeedback: A sign holding across a cut means an even multiplicity. Both (x − 7) and (x − 4) appear once here, so the sign changes at both.

explanationVariants: x + 6/x = 5 (LCD x): x² + 6 = 5x → x² − 5x + 6 = 0 → (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0: x = 2 or 3, both legal (neither is 0).
Clearing can raise the degree — factor the quadratic, then filter.

commonBuilds.feedback: Check 3 too: 3 + 6/3 = 3 + 2 = 5 ✓ — both survive; only x = 0 was banned.
Don't drop the 6/x — clearing gives x² + 6 = 5x, a QUADRATIC with roots 2 and 3.
x² − 5x + 6 needs factors summing to +5: (x − 2)(x − 3) — positive roots.
x² − 5x + 6 needs factors summing to +5: (x − 2)(x − 3) — positive roots.

widget.missFeedback: Multiply through by x: x² + 6 = 5x, so x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 — then check both against x ≠ 0.
widget.successFeedback: Right — x² − 5x + 6 = 0 factors as (x − 2)(x − 3); neither candidate zeroes the denominator.

explanationVariants: 3/(x − 1) = (x + 2)/(x − 1) forces 3 = x + 2 → x = 1 — but 1 is BANNED: no solution.
When the only candidate is the excluded value, the solution set is empty.

options.label: no solution — the only candidate is excluded
options.feedback: Right — matching denominators force x = 1, which zeroes them: empty set.

options.label: x = 1
options.feedback: Substitute: 3/0 — undefined; the candidate dies at the door.

options.label: x = 5
options.feedback: Equal denominators equate the TOPS: 3 = x + 2 → x = 1 (then the ban strikes).

options.label: x = −2
options.feedback: Equating the matching-denominator tops gives 3 = x + 2 → x = 1 (which is banned), never −2.

explanationVariants: 2/(x − 2) = x/(x − 2) − 1: clear by (x − 2): 2 = x − (x − 2) = 2 — TRUE for every legal x! Every x except 2 solves it.
The cleared equation is an identity; only the exclusion carves the solution set.

options.label: every real x except 2
options.feedback: Right — clearing gives 2 = x − x + 2, always true; only the ban at 2 limits it.

options.label: x = 2 only
options.feedback: 2 is the one value that CAN'T work — it zeroes the denominators.

options.label: no solution
options.feedback: Test x = 5: 2/3 vs 5/3 − 1 = 2/3 ✓ — the cleared equation holds everywhere legal.

options.label: x = 0 only
options.feedback: 0 works (−1 = −1 ✓) — but so does every other x ≠ 2: the identity admits them all.

hints: 2 = 2: an identity — true for all x except the banned 2.

steps.body: Clear by the LCD, solve, then filter candidates against the banned list.
takeaways: LCD-clearing can mint phantoms at denominator zeros — always check.
Clearing may raise the degree: expect quadratics.
Identities solve to 'everything except the exclusions'; contradictions to nothing.

concept.body: The smallest case: 6/x = 3. Multiply both sides by x: 6 = 3x.

commonErrors.feedback: 6 = 3x solves to x = 2 — the x was UNDER the 6, so it ends up as 6/3.
